messages.subject: Creating bins in R
parts:
Hello,

I am having trouble figuring out the code for binning data in R (apologies from an ignorant R user). I saw to use the create.bins() function but am confused about how to code the vector for the cutpoints. I am needing it to be from 0-100 m in 10m steps. Also, once the bins are set, how do you include this argument into the ds() function?

messages.author: f2122b34f1aa6e95
messages.subject: Re: [distance-sampling] Creating bins in R
parts:
Hi John:

Here's a simple example using the "minke" dataset provided in the
Distance R package, containing exact distances:

library(Distance)
data(minke) # makes dataset available in workspace
# next line sets the cutpoints between bins
# read ds() documentation to note that the sequence
# must include 0 and the maximum distance, number of bins=num.cutpts - 1
# in your situation you would want seq(0,100,by=10)
cutpts <- seq(0, max(minke$distance, na.rm=TRUE), length=10)
# having set the cutpoints, argument 'cutpoints' makes use of them
test <- ds(minke, cutpoints = cutpts)
plot(test)

messages.subject: Re: [distance-sampling] Creating bins in R
parts:
Hi John, hi listfolk,

I think this can be fixed by updating the version of dsm on your machine
to the version currently on github.

This can be done either by downloading the file "dsm_2.2.11-windows.zip"
(but ensuring you rename it to dsm_2.2.11.zip first) from:

https://github.com/DistanceDevelopment/dsm/releases/tag/2.2.11

and choosing Tools>Install packages "install from local archive" then
select your file in RStudio or by typing

install.packages(devtools)
devtools::install_github("DistanceDevelopment/dsm")

at the R prompt.

Calling library(dsm) in a new session should then yield: "This is dsm
2.2.11"

If this bug persists, please do send me a note and a minimal example of
code to reproduce the error and I'll take a look.

Hope this helps!

cheers,
--dave

I am having the same problem as John Edwards. I tried using the same code as described above by Eric, but I continue to get the same problem. I ran my dataset in program DISTANCE v7  such that the dataset had blank/empty cells for distance and cluster size for points with no detections. In program DISTANCE I set cut points at 0, 25, 50, and 100 to reflect distance bins. We didn't measure actual distance, so in the dataset I used the midpoint distance for each bin as the distance (e.g., 13, 38, 63, 88; distanceX in attached). The best fit model in program distance was a uniform cosine (1, 2) model. The data have 78 points, with 124 rows.

I am trying to recreate the model in R, but I cannot set the cutpoints because there are NAs in the data at points we did not detect birds.
I tried this code:

    cutpts<-seq(0, max(100, na.rm=TRUE), length=5)   ##Note, I cannot use data$dista
    test <- ds(distdata, cutpoints = cutpts)
    plot(test)

I also tried recoding the distances to the max values of the bins such that distance was either blank, 25, 50, 75, or 100 (distance in attached). Then used this code:
  
    cutpts<-seq(0, max(distdata$distance, na.rm=TRUE), length=5)   ##Note, I cannot use data$dista
    test <- ds(distdata, cutpoints = cutpts)
    plot(test)

Both result in the desired cutpts of 0, 25, 50, 75, and 100, but both give the error:
   
    Error in create.bins(data, cutpoints) :
    Some distances are NA, can't create bins.

And when I subsequently try to run the model:

    df_unifcos2 <- ds(data=distdata, key="unif", cutpoints=cutpts, adjustment = "cos", order = c(1, 2))
    summary(df_unifcos2)

I get the same error. The model runs, ignoring the cutpoints, but the results are very different from those produced in the DISTANCE v. 7 program. I don't know what to do to get matching models in both R and DISTANCE v. 7.

Any suggestions?

messages.subject: Re: {Filename?} Re: [distance-sampling] Creating bins in R
parts:
- From your earlier correspondence, I believe you have point transect data.  You'll need to inform the ds() function of this fact using the "transect" argument.

- Also, acquire the latest version of the Distance package from github, as there have been a few refinements to the create.bins() function.

devtools::install_github("DistanceDevelopment/Distance")

- Filter the distances being sent to the ds() function (and then to the create.bins() function) this way (see example for create.bins()):

test <- ds(distdata[!is.na(distdata$distance),], transect="point",
           key="unif", adjustment="cos", order=c(1,2),
           cutpoints = cutpts)

This leads to a "no models fit" message, so a glance at a histogram of the data is enlightening


It will be a challenge to fit a detection function to these data.
